author: jim-hightower
Original: Once upon a time, conservative ideologues opposed government interference in the holy magic of the marketplace. Take energy policy, for example. Right-wing cheerleaders of fossil fuels demanded that the government keep its fat thumb off the scale of free market competition between Big Oil and those frilly new "alternative" sources of energy.

author: david-harsanyi
Original: During a recent town hall, a Michigan University student named Iman Dashti confronted Democratic Party's Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed regarding his habitual whitewashing and rationalization of Islamic terrorism. Dashti, who says his family is a victim of the Iranian regime's theocratic persecution, pressed the candidate numerous times to denounce one of the world's most odious tyrannies.

author: veronique-de-rugy
Original: Inflation hasn't gone away — it's going up. With the midterm elections seven weeks off, that's a problem for the president and Congress. Voters hate inflation. They don't much like the cure either, and the cure has two parts. The Federal Reserve raising interest rates, like it just did, is one. The second part is overlooked and in the hands of Congress. Indeed, the Fed can't bring inflation down for good unless lawmakers show they will back the debt with future fiscal surpluses. That means becoming serious about overspending.

author: chuck-norris
Original: Democrats are the masters of deceptive persuasion, meaning they will take our attention off something they have really screwed up and put it on something that's not quite so bad. And chief among those masters is he who resides at 1600 Pennsylvania Ave. in Washington, D.C.

author: jamie-stiehm
Original: What a glorious day in June. The Barack Obama Presidential Center opening in Chicago gave us a complete contradiction of the times we've been living through. Community rather than chaos, lightness versus darkness, and hope instead of fear.

author: jim-hightower
Original: I've got to hand it to Washington's Republican policymakers. They've come up with a truly remarkable way that, they promise, will vastly expand the number of small businesses in America. Great! This is personal for me, for I grew up in a family that had a Main Street business in small-town Texas, so I know how hard it is for little guys to battle the raw monopoly power of corporate chains. Thus, I cheered the GOP ... until I learned that their small business proposal is just another big business scam.

author: connie-schultz
Original: Perhaps I should start with a story. I first met Michael J. Fox in 2006, not long after Rush Limbaugh had mocked his involuntary movements caused by Parkinson's disease. Michael was in Ohio for a rally in support of stem cell research that could save countless lives.

author: jim-hightower
Original: Likewise, calling a small group of partisan lawyers a "supreme" court doesn't make it one. There's nothing supreme about the six-pack of far-right-wing political activists who are presently soiling our people's ideals of justice by proclaiming their own anti-democratic biases to be the law of the land. On issues of economic fairness, women's rights, racial justice, corporate supremacy, environmental protection, theocratic rule and other fundamentals, these unelected, black-robed extremists are imposing an illegitimate elitist agenda on America that the people do not want and ultimately will not tolerate.

author: lawrence-kudlow
Original: The Trump administration and the Republicans in Congress have passed one of the best pro-growth tax bills ever. The Tax Cuts and Jobs Act ranks in the all-time hall of fame along with former President Reagan's 1981 and 1986 tax acts, and former President Kennedy's posthumous tax cuts in 1964. The announcements by Apple, FedEx, AT&T, Fiat Chrysler and over 300 companies with multibillion dollar investments in the United States are early lead indicators of good things to come from the tax-rate cuts.

author: connie-schultz
Original: Evolution at work: A Cheney told the truth in public. The Wyoming congresswoman, 54, took a lonely stand by defying former President Donald Trump's "big lie," as she put it, that the 2020 election victory was stolen. There's no room for truth in her party.

author: david-harsanyi
Original: Why didn't President Donald Trump initially want to share the full text of the framework agreement between the United States and the Islamic Republic of Iran? The first reason is obvious: The memorandum of understanding is a capitulation to the clerics of the regime.

author: connie-schultz
Original: There are many reasons to reflect on the historical significance of President Joe Biden's first joint address to Congress. It was a great speech by a man who understands why he is in this role, in this time. He knows who we need him to be, and isn't that a relief.

author: froma-harrop
Original: It would be hard to find a more insulting offer than to exchange money for your vote. That's exactly what President Donald Trump did in announcing that if voters keep Republicans in power come the midterms, he'll send every adult citizen a $5,000 check.

author: veronique-de-rugy
Original: Most Americans apparently agree on at least one thing. Unfortunately, it's something dangerous: price controls. A new Wall Street Journal poll finds remarkable bipartisan support for government limits on prices, with 93% of Democrats and 83% of Republicans supporting capping prescription drug prices. Nearly four in five voters support capping credit card interest rates at 10%. And large majorities favor capping child care charges for working families.

author: marc-dion
Original: "'I'm dreadin' what I've got to watch,' the Colour-Sergeant said." Rudyard Kipling, the racist poet of the British Empire and the writer of the made-into-cartoons "Jungle Book," wrote those words in a poem called "Danny Deever," a poem about a British soldier being hung for murdering a fellow soldier in 1890, in India.
